title: When Temptation Comes From Those We Love

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you love, or your closest friend secretly entices you, saying, "Let us go and worship other gods" (gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods of the peoples around you, whether near or far, from one end of the land to the other), do not yield to him or listen to him. Show him no pity. Do not spare him or shield him. - Deut 13:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God addresses one of the hardest tests of loyalty: what if the person urging you toward idolatry is someone you deeply love — a brother, a child, a spouse, a closest friend? These are the people whose words carry the most weight with us, whose influence reaches deepest into our hearts. And precisely because we love them, their pull toward wrong can be the hardest to resist. God's command is clear: even then, "do not yield." Loyalty to God must come before loyalty to anyone, even those dearest to us.

This is a searching truth. Our closest relationships have enormous power to shape the direction of our faith, for good or ill. Sometimes the strongest temptations to compromise come not from strangers but from those we love most, who may draw us — even unintentionally — away from wholehearted devotion to God. Love for people must never become an excuse to abandon our love for God.

Jesus spoke with similar seriousness: "Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me" (Matt 10:37). He was not commanding us to stop loving our families — He calls us to love them deeply. But He must hold first place. When human love competes with our devotion to God, God comes first. This is not cold-heartedness; ultimately, keeping God first is the most loving thing we can do, for ourselves and for those we love. If someone dear is pulling you away from God, hold fast to Him. Keeping God first will make your other loves truer, not weaker.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do my closest relationships draw me toward God or pull me away from Him?
- Have I ever let love for someone become an excuse to compromise with God?
- What does it mean to keep God first even above those I love most?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You must hold first place in my heart, even above those I love most. Give me the strength to hold fast to You when someone dear pulls me away, and help me love others rightly by loving You first of all. Amen.
